newsitem.title: USA: U.S. military college plans disciplinary hearings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. military college plans disciplinary hearings.

text.p: The Citadel military college said Friday it would hold disciplinary hearings for 11 male cadets charged with violating regulations in connection with alleged hazing of two former female cadets.

The hearings, now set for Saturday, had been scheduled for Feb. 22, but were postponed when parents and cadets complained about "the extensive questioning" by attorneys for the U.S. Department of Justice, the school said in a statement.
Fifteen cadets were charged in connection with the hazing. Three have left the school and a fourth has been disciplined.

The Citadel said that two Commandant's Board sessions and nine hearings were scheduled for Saturday and would be closed to the press and public. The school said it expects results by March 7 and would have no comment until then.

Two women cadets, Kim Messer and Jeanie Mentavlos, withdrew from the Citadel in January. The two women, who were among four women enrolled at the state-funded school after it changed its all-male admissions policy last summer, had alleged they were victims of severe hazing and harassment.
Among other things, they had claimed they were sprayed with fingernail polish remover and then set on fire.
